step1_analysis.description: A complementary cross-coupled CMOS pair that provides negative resistance. It is typically used as the active core of an LC voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) to sustain oscillation, or as a bistable latch in digital circuits.

paper_reference.title: A Fully Integrated SONET OC-48 Transceiver in Standard CMOS

oscillation_frequency.description: Fundamental oscillation frequency of the VCO when loaded with an LC tank.

sky130_expected.calculation: f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). With an ideal L=2nH and C=2pF added in the testbench, f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(4e-21)) = 2.516 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined primarily by the ideal LC tank components added in the testbench, with minor downward shifts due to the parasitic capacitances of the cross-coupled transistors.

negative_resistance.description: Small-signal negative resistance provided by the cross-coupled pair to overcome tank losses and sustain oscillation.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm_n = 2*Id/Vov ~= 1.3mS. gm_p ~= 0.24mS. G_neg = -(gm_n + gm_p)/2 = -0.77mS. R_neg = 1/G_neg = -1300 ohms.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated from the transconductance of the cross-coupled NMOS and PMOS transistors biased at the metastable point (VDD/2).

power_consumption.description: DC power consumed by the cross-coupled pair during steady-state oscillation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Average current drawn from 1.8V supply during oscillation. Estimated at ~1-2mA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The VCO core consumes only a small fraction of the total transceiver power. The current is determined by the dynamic switching of the cross-coupled pair.

oscillation_amplitude.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing at the oscillator output nodes.

sky130_expected.calculation: Swing is limited by the supply voltage and transistors entering the triode region.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The inductor allows the node voltages to swing above VDD and below GND, typically reaching 2-3V peak-to-peak differentially.

phase_noise.description: Phase noise of the oscillator at a specific offset frequency.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Phase noise depends heavily on the Q-factor of the LC tank. With ideal components, it would be artificially low. Not measured in this basic testbench.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench for the cross-coupled VCO core. It adds an ideal LC tank (2nH, 2pF) to set the oscillation frequency to ~2.5 GHz. It performs an AC analysis to measure the small-signal negative resistance at resonance, and a transient analysis (kickstarted by a brief current pulse) to measure oscillation frequency, amplitude, and power consumption.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Fully Integrated SONET OC-48 Transceiver - VCO Core
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* DUT
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u

XM3 QP QN VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 QN QP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM1 QP QN GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 QN QP GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}

* Testbench components
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
L1 QP QN 2nH
C1 QP QN 2pF

* Kickstart current pulse for Tran (single pulse), AC source for AC analysis
Ikick QP QN PULSE(0 1m 0 100p 100p 100p 100n) AC 1

.control
* 1. AC Analysis for Negative Resistance
ac dec 100 1G 10G
let v_diff_ac = v(QP) - v(QN)
let z_mag = mag(v_diff_ac)
meas ac z_max max z_mag
let neg_res = -z_max
print neg_res

* 2. Transient Analysis for Oscillation
tran 10p 50n
* Measure frequency (using cycles near the end of simulation to ensure steady-state)
meas tran t1 trig v(QP) val=0.9 rise=1 from=40n to=50n
meas tran t2 trig v(QP) val=0.9 rise=2 from=40n to=50n
let osc_freq = 1 / (t2 - t1)
print osc_freq

* Measure amplitude
meas tran vqp_max max v(QP) from=40n to=50n
meas tran vqp_min min v(QP) from=40n to=50n
let vqp_pp = vqp_max - vqp_min
print vqp_pp

* Measure power
meas tran pwr_avg avg i(VVDD) from=40n to=50n
let power_mW = -pwr_avg * 1.8 * 1000
print power_mW

quit
.endc
.end
